data.title: Palantir Stocks Decline 4.94% Before an 11.7% Sequential Revenue Growth Test
data.description:
Palantir , which supplies AI software to businesses and government agencies, faces a demanding earnings hurdle. Shares declined 4.94% to $186.72 at 11:25 am ET on October 30, despite fresh brokerage backing. JPMorgan initiated Overweight coverage with a $262 target on October 29, according to AD HOC NEWS. The next test arrives November 2, when Palantir reports after the U.S. close.

The numbers leave little room to coast. Palantir's August guidance called for September-quarter revenue of $2.160 billion$2.164 billion and adjusted operating income of $1.292 billion$1.296 billion. Against approximately $1.935 billion in preceding-quarter revenue, that midpoint demands roughly 11.7% sequential growth. The operating-income midpoint also implies an adjusted operating margin near 60%, giving investors two clear benchmarks to check.

The valuation raises the stakes. GuruFocus shows a GF Score of 84 out of 100, with growth and momentum standing out, but a price-to-earnings ratio of 159.05 and price-to-book ratio of 45.88 suggest substantial expectations remain embedded in the price. Delivering the revenue target could reinforce the expansion story; sustaining that valuation may require another convincing outlook. The $262 target offers an optimistic reference point, but revenue, margins and forward guidance will give investors firmer ground.

data.title: Parvis Sharpens Focus on Profitability and Canadian Platform Integration; Terminates FavorPoint Capital Purchase Agreement
data.description:
Disciplined capital allocation prioritizes integration of Atlas One and a clear path to profitability

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 30, 2026) - Parvis Invest Inc. ("Parvis" or the "Company"), a technology-driven platform for private alternative investments, today announced that it has terminated the share purchase agreement to acquire FavorPoint Capital, LLC ("FavorPoint"), a FINRA-registered broker-dealer headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, and will defer its planned U.S. expansion. The decision reflects the Company's commitment to disciplined capital allocation and to maximizing the value of the strategic acquisitions completed earlier this year.

The TSX Venture Exchange (the "Exchange") has not yet completed its review of the proposed transaction. Rather than continue to commit resources to an uncertain timeline, and after consultation with investors and careful assessment of current market conditions, the Board of Directors and management concluded that shareholders are best served by concentrating the Company's capital, people and attention on its Canadian platform, where Parvis has built significant scale and momentum in 2026.

A Stronger, More Focused Parvis

With the acquisitions and integrations of Atlas One Digital Securities and Richmond Global Wealth, Parvis has assembled what the Company believes is one of Canada's most comprehensive investment platforms. Redirecting resources previously earmarked for the U.S. transaction allows the Company to capture the full operating synergies of its integrated platform sooner. It also eliminates the near-term operating, legal and regulatory costs associated with entering a new jurisdiction. The Company can now prioritize revenue growth and a clear path to profitability in its core Canadian market. At the same time, Parvis preserves its balance-sheet flexibility and the optionality to revisit U.S. opportunities from a position of greater strength.

Fiscal Update

For the six months ended September 30, 2026, the Company generated revenue of $1,386,510, up 21.0% from $1,146,249 in the same period last year. Consolidated net income was $335,000, and normalized EBITDA was $369,544, compared to negative $88,906 a year earlier. Normalized EBITDA reflects the earnings of the Company's core exempt market dealer business before one-time costs and professional fees at the parent company level related to the reorganization of the Company's entities after recent acquisitions. All financial information in this section is unaudited and remains subject to completion of the Company's interim financial report and management's discussion and analysis for the six months ended September 30, 2026, to be filed on SEDAR+.

Atlas One Integration Complete

Parvis has completed the integration of Atlas One, which closed on August 13, 2026, across all legal, regulatory, technology and personnel work streams. Atlas One has been amalgamated with Parvis Investment Services Inc., the Company's wholly owned registered exempt market dealer, uniting Atlas One's issuer network and national investor base with the Parvis platform under a single registered dealer. Atlas One's dealing representatives have joined the Parvis exempt market dealer network, all investors now onboard through a single digital interface, and Atlas One's active issuers and offerings have been migrated onto the Parvis platform. The combined proprietary platform serves more than 65 active issuers and a network of over 17,000 qualified investors across Canada. With integration complete, one of the assumptions underlying the Company's fiscal 2027 guidance has been satisfied, and management's attention now turns fully to growing revenue and delivering the Company's first full year of profitability.

"We transformed Parvis this year through two acquisitions, and the value we create now comes from executing on that combined platform in Canada," said David Michaud, Founder and CEO of Parvis. "Atlas One is fully integrated, and our focus is delivering our first full year of profitability. The U.S. remains a long-term opportunity, and we will be in a stronger position to pursue it from a profitable Canadian platform. We thank the FavorPoint team for their professionalism throughout the process."

Termination of Agreement & Concurrent Financing

The purchase agreement was terminated by mutual written consent among all parties on October 29, 2026. As a result, the Company will not proceed with the remaining tranches of its previously announced convertible debenture financing (the "Concurrent Financing"), announced May 28, 2026 and amended June 30, 2026, which were principally intended to fund the FavorPoint acquisition. The first tranche of the Concurrent Financing remains outstanding in accordance with its terms, and its proceeds have been applied to the Atlas One integration and working capital, consistent with prior disclosure. The Company expects its current cash position and operating cash flow to be sufficient to fund its operations.

About Parvis

Parvis is a full-service private markets firm, pairing a technology-driven distribution platform with dedicated advisory to expand access to institutional-quality opportunities. In 2025, Parvis raised over $200 million (inclusive of Atlas One) for private market investments, demonstrating the scale and reach of its platform. Headquartered in Vancouver, Parvis operates across Canada with teams in Toronto, Vancouver, and Montreal. The Company (via its subsidiary) is registered as an exempt market dealer under NI 31-103 and listed on the TSX Venture Exchange . For more information, visit www.parvisinvest.com and SEDAR+.

data.title: SRX Global Provides Update on Balance Sheet and Share Buyback
data.description:
NORTH PALM BEACH, Fla., Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SRX Global Inc. (NYSE American: SRXH) (the “Company” or “SRX”), an AI-enabled platform dedicated to generating long-term shareholder value through investments in high-conviction operating companies and strategic assets, today is providing shareholders with an update on its balance sheet and share buyback.

As of October 30, 2026, the Company has approximately $34 million in aggregate cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term U.S. Treasury bills. The Company does not have any exposure to cryptocurrency as of today. These balances are preliminary, unaudited, based on currently available information and subject to adjustment upon completion of applicable accounting and reconciliation procedures. They do not represent September 30, 2026 fiscal year-end balances or a complete presentation of the Company’s financial condition. The Company currently expects to report its fiscal year-end results and file its Annual Report on Form 10-K in early December 2026.

Additionally, the Company has been actively utilizing its stock repurchase program as of today’s release. The program permits repurchases of up to the lesser of 10 million shares or 50% of its issued and outstanding common stock at any given time, for an aggregate purchase price not exceeding $20 million, through July 7, 2027. Future repurchases are subject to market conditions, available capital and applicable legal requirements.

The Company expects to disclose the total number of shares repurchased and the average price paid for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 when it reports its fiscal year-end results in early December 2026.

data.title: JioStar's Q2 profit falls 13% amid weak ad environment
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 30 -- Reliance Industries Ltd's entertainment subsidiary JioStar reported a 10% year-on-year jump in revenue to Rs.6,806 crore in the September quarter, although earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (Ebitda) fell nearly 14% to Rs.1,502 crore.

Profits after tax for the quarter stood at Rs.1,147 crore, down 13% on-year.

The company said a "weak ad environment" hurt the quarter, although subscription and streaming revenue helped boost overall revenue. However, linear TV ad revenue remained "under transition", it added.

Sports ad revenue increased as more cricket events were held this quarter, including the England-India bilateral series held in July.

RIL does not break out JioStar's revenue by segments.

JioHotstar's monthly active users (MAUs) surged to 530 million in the June quarter, driven by the Indian Premier League, but fell to 440 million in the September quarter. However, the figure remained above the 400 million recorded in the year-ago quarter.

It remains a goal for JioStar to retain users from the typical Q1 surge in viewership driven by the IPL.

Overall, while JioStar's revenue is up 12% to Rs.20,743 crore for the first half of fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27), Ebitda fell 7.4% to Rs.2,551 crore and Ebitda margins contracted to 14.4% from 17.5% a year ago. Profits after tax for the first half of the year stood at Rs.1,812 crore, down nearly 5% on-year.

JioStar also expanded its JioHotstar streaming service into new international markets, including the UK, Canada, and Singapore, during the quarter, while the platform's flagship reality TV show, Bigg Boss, launched versions in six languages simultaneously, reaching 90 million streaming viewers in the first three weeks.

Heavy investments in sports and struggle to attract ad revenue in a disrupted consumer market have hit margins for all major entertainment networks. Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd also reported a 40% on-year decline in profits after tax as the company invested heavily in broadcast and streaming rights for FIFA World Cup and other events for an eight-year period. Zee's ad revenue for the quarter was flat on-year.

data.title: Valero to Buy Shuttered Lyondell Houston Refinery; Restart by 2027 — OPIS
data.description:
* Valero Energy will pay $320.5 million for the LyondellBasell Houston

refinery.

* The company hopes to restart the facility sometime next year.

* The refinery had an estimated crude processing capacity of 289,000 b/d

before its March 2025 shutdown.

Valero Energy said it agreed to buy the former Houston refinery owned by

LyondellBasell and expects to initially restart the facility's 165,000 b/d of

light-sweet crude processing capacity by the end of 2027, marking the first

restart of a shuttered production facility in decades.

Analysts said Valero's latest acquisition would give the U.S. refiner an option

to process more heavy crudes when the volumes of those slates are expected to

increase. In addition, they said the refinery on the Houston Ship Channel will

also provide valuable storage and loading facilities to improve Valero's

ability to export products and access different crudes.

Valero said in a press statement the acquisition, for a price of $320.5

million, will also allow it to invest in high-complexity, heavy sour crude

processing at the refinery in the future. The deal is expected to complete by

the end of this year, subject to customary closing conditions, the company

said.

LyondellBasell's Houston refinery had an estimated total crude processing

capacity of 289,000 b/d before the company shut its operations in March 2025,

citing the global petrochemicals company's decision to exit the oil refining

business.

The acquisition also includes the Houston refinery's 13.5 million barrels of

storage capacity and extensive logistics infrastructure including marine docks,

rail loading facilities, and truck racks, Valero said in an investor

presentation.

Valero said it expects to deal to be "accretive," or profitable, in the first

year of operations, "with additional upside from future heavy sour crude

processing investment."

In addition, Valero said the refinery's incremental fluid catalytic cracking

and hydrocracker feed production would reduce its reliance on third-party

feedstock sourcing. The refinery's excess hydrotreating capacity would allow

upgrading of intermediates from other Valero U.S. Gulf Coast refineries, it

said.

Matthew Blair, Tudor, Pickering & Holt's head of chemicals, refiners and

renewable fuels equity research, said the deal valuation was attractive. This

is because the valuation of the initial additional light-sweet crude capacity

represents just a fraction of the replacement value considered where WTI crude

contracts are currently trading.

However, LyondellBasell had previously said it would take at least a $1 billion

turnaround to keep the refinery running, and Blair noted it could cost an

estimated $3 billion to get the plant up to Valero's standards.

Theresa Chen, North American midstream and refining analyst at Barclays, said

the Houston refinery's logistics infrastructure has significant integration

opportunities with Valero's existing Gulf Coast footprint.

She said that complex U.S. Gulf Coast refineries that are processing the

relatively cheaper heavy crudes should remain "economically insulated," even in

an oversupplied market after Russian and Middle East refining capacity

eventually returns to service.

Within the past 12 months, both Phillips 66's 147,000 b/d Los Angeles and

Valero's 150,000 b/d Benicia refineries were shut, with the oil companies

citing a difficult operating environment in California.

Last week, Valero's General Counsel Joe Walsh said in an analysis that the

company has no plans to restart the Benicia refinery.

In recent years, refiners like ExxonMobil and Marathon Petroleum have invested

in relatively smaller projects in their existing refineries to improve the

yields of higher-value products. In 2023, ExxonMobil completed its expansion of

the Beaumont, Texas, refinery that added 250,000 b/d of crude processing

capacity.

Valero is the second-largest U.S. refinery operator with a total throughput

capacity of 3 million b/d. It operates 14 refineries in the U.S., Canada and

the U.K., as well as 12 ethanol plants in the U.S. with 1.7 billion gallons per

year of production capacity.

data.title: Isabella Bank 3Q 2026: Revenue $23.9M, EPS $0.86— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Isabella Bank Corp reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $23.9 million, up 16.7% year over year, and net income of $6.6 million, up 26%. Diluted EPS increased to $0.86 from $0.71 as higher loan and securities yields and lower deposit costs lifted net interest income and margin.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $23.9M, compared with $20.5M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 16.7%.
  • Net income was $6.6M, compared with $5.2M; YoY change 26.0%.
  • Diluted EPS was $0.86, compared with $0.71; YoY change 21.1%.
  • Net interest income rose to $19.4M from $16.2M, while net interest margin (FTE) increased to 3.71% from 3.15%.

Business Highlights

  • For the first nine months of 2026, net income rose year over year to $16.6M and net interest income increased to $54.3M. Service fees and wealth management fees also grew.
  • Commercial real estate and residential real estate loans expanded, while mortgage-broker advances and consumer loans declined.
  • Money market and savings balances grew, offsetting declines in certificates of deposit and demand deposits.
  • The company signed a merger agreement with Grand River Commerce. Integration, cost savings and customer retention remain uncertain.

Original SEC Filing: ISABELLA BANK CORP [ ISBA ] - 10-Q - Oct. 30, 2026

data.title: Reddit Stocks Decline 28% With AI Search Pressuring Audience Growth
data.description:
Reddit , the community and advertising platform, faces a tough balancing act: protect its advertising engine without driving visitors away. Shares sank 28.1% to $93.18 at 11:30 a.m. ET on October 30 as investors weighed weaker search traffic and planned login tests. The platform's proposed access changes could help protect its content, but management warned that daily users could weaken if October's search-referral trend continues.

The pressure sits squarely in Reddit's biggest revenue market. U.S. revenue reached $719 million of the $895 million global total, even as U.S. daily active users decreased 2% from a year earlier to 50.7 million. Its shareholder letter said logged-in and app engagement generated more than 80% of monetization, while fourth-quarter revenue guidance stood at $1.0 billion$1.03 billion. With the United States contributing roughly 80.3% of revenue, keeping valuable users engaged could matter more than protecting the headline audience count.

The selloff comes with a mixed financial picture. GuruFocus shows a GF Score of 47 out of 100, with stronger growth and financial strength offset by weaker profitability, valuation and momentum readings. Trading volume of 15.69 million shares already exceeded three times the two-month average of 4.87 million, underscoring the intensity of the reaction. Login requirements could strengthen user identification and advertising targeting, but every extra step risks losing casual visitors. Reddit now needs to show that tighter access can preserve engagement and support its revenue outlook while search traffic softens.

  • AbbVie’s Q3 revenue rose 10.3% to $17.40 billion, driven by over 16% growth in its immunology business.
  • AbbVie raised its FY 2026 revenue forecast to $67.8 billion from $67.6 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95 - $13.99 from $13.76 - $13.96.

Shares of Eli Lilly (LLY) and AbbVie (ABBV) climbed to new record highs on Friday after the pharmaceutical behemoths reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings and raised their full-year 2026 outlooks.

LLY stock was up 3.5% at the time of writing, extending its gains to a fifth straight session. It is on track to post its biggest monthly gains since November 2025. Meanwhile, ABBV shares rose 1.6%.

Wall Street Sees Upside For LLY After Q3 Earnings Beat

Analysts turned bullish on Eli Lilly (LLY) on Friday, betting on its obesity-drug leadership and expanding pipeline. Scotiabank raised its target to $1,605 from $1,300 and held an ‘Outperform’ rating, expecting Lilly to maintain its obesity-market dominance through ‘next-generation products’ and acquisitions.

Truist lifted its target to $1,612 from $1,376, and maintained a ‘Buy’ rating. The firm said Lilly currently has only about 10% market penetration in obesity, and expansion of its incretin franchise and pipeline will cement its dominance in “diabesity” for years to come.

On Thursday, Lilly reported a 39% increase in Q3 revenue to $24.4 billion, while adjusted earnings rose 7% to $7.48 per share. Mounjaro sales surged 65% to $10.72 billion, while Zepbound revenue rose 49% to $5.35 billion. Lilly also raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $91 billion-$92 billion from $85 billion-$87 billion. However, the company trimmed its bottom-line guidance to $35-$36 per share from $35.5-$36.5 per share.

UBS said Lilly’s underlying momentum and a higher Q4 growth run rate could potentially make current estimates appear too conservative.

Retail sentiment surrounding LLY on Stocktwits turned ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ a day earlier. The stock has gained more than 31% so far in 2026.

AbbVie Raises FY26 Outlook

AbbVie reported better-than-expected Q3 earnings on Friday, driven by strong growth in its immunology business.

Revenue rose 10.3% to $17.40 billion, beating Wall Street’s estimates of $17.34 billion, according to Fiscal.ai. Adjusted earnings more than doubled to $3.82 per share, exceeding consensus estimates of $3.77 per share.

Immunology revenue increased 16.3%, with Skyrizi, its autoimmune drug for psoriatic arthritis and Crohn’s disease, among others, generating $5.78 billion. Rinvoq, prescribed for inflammatory conditions including rheumatoid arthritis and eczema, saw sales surge nearly 24%.

AbbVie also raised its FY 2026 revenue forecast to $67.8 billion from $67.6 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95 - $13.99 from $13.76 - $13.96.

In a call with analysts, chief scientific officer Roopal Thakkar said the company is interested in expanding its obesity-treatment pipeline, according to The Fly.

Meanwhile, retail sentiment for ABBV on Stocktwits remained ‘neutral’ over the past 24 hours. The stock has gained about 29% in 2026.

data.title: North Korean hackers linked to crypto thefts among world's best, experts say
data.description:
By AJ Vicens

North Korean hackers likely behind the record $6.3 billion theft from cryptocurrency exchange Binance are among the world's most prolific crypto thieves, and the proceeds help fund the country's weapons programs, cybersecurity experts said on Friday.

Blockchain investigation firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attribute the heist to a North Korean hacking group known as “TraderTraitor,” a name used in a 2022 joint warning from the FBI, CISA and US Treasury that described how hackers used malicious software and other tricks to target software developers and IT staff at cryptocurrency companies.

North Korea stole at least $6.75 billion in cryptocurrency through the end of 2025, Chainalysis said in a December 2025 report. That total includes the $1.5 billion ByBitexchange hack in February 2025.

The group also hit Bitget, a separate exchange, taking $387 million in September, experts have said, bringing the minimum total of cryptocurrency North Korea has stolen to roughly $13.5 billion, said Michael Barnhart, a researcher with cybersecurity firm DTEX.

Binance said it and others were working to freeze some of the stolen cryptocurrency, with about $3 billion located so far.

“After Bitget, a lot of the community expected something like this,” Barnhart said.

TraderTraitor is North Korea’s “most capable hacking group with a primary focus on financials and one staffed by some of the most experienced operators in the regime’s cyber programs in the former APT38 ranks,” he added, referring to North Korea’s long-running financially focused hacking units.

Researchers say TraderTraitor targets developers and IT staff at financial institutions through malware or phony job offers, tricking candidates into downloading malicious software during fake job interviews, giving the hackers access to login credentials and other sensitive data.

Rafe Pilling, a senior director of threat research at Sophos, said early reports of how the hackers compromised Binance match the North Korean playbook, and that the group is expert at working out how a company's systems and staff approve money transfers. "This group in particular are somewhat artists in terms of getting into these distributed finance companies," he said.

FROM CRYPTO THEFT TO WEAPONS FUNDING

After stealing the money, the hackers pass it to Chinese organized crime money-laundering groups, Barnhart said.

North Koreans also secretly take jobs at tech and financial companies in the US and other countries to earn money to send back to the North Korean government and steal sensitive data, the FBI said in an October 13 public service announcement,adding that money raised by the workers and hackers helps fund North Korean nuclear and military programs.

A US State Department spokesman said North Korean cybercrime is a “global problem” and that the country has “increasingly turned to cybercrime to circumvent international sanctions and fund its unlawful weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs. Cryptocurrency heists and laundering have become a significant part of this strategy.”

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has called for the country to seize "absolute superiority" in drone and other military technology, and the drone program's gains are directly tied to the heists and the overseas IT worker schemes, Barnhart said.

The country is also aiding Russia’s war effort, he added.

“North Korea has sent troops, munitions, and weapons components to Russia, all funded through the same system, which is why a crypto hack is a national security issue and not only a problem for the exchange that got hit,” Barnhart said.

data.title: The Fed Is Focused on Inflation, but the Labor Market Needs Attention, Too — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Megan Leonhardt

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh devoted just a few words to the labor market at his news conference on Oct. 28, assuring the audience that employment conditions are stable. "Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little, so on the employment side of the Fed's dual mandate, conditions are quite positive," he said, before pivoting to a discussion of inflation.

Yet the labor outlook may not be as rosy as Warsh suggested. Payroll growth is noticeably above last year's pace, but this year's average monthly gain of 68,000 isn't especially strong, and the drivers behind sluggish job growth aren't fading.

Policymakers can't afford to ignore the weakness. Higher short-term interest rates may help to cool inflation, but they could put further strain on the labor market's health.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics is set to release October's employment data on Nov. 6. Economists project that employers added 55,000 jobs to payrolls in the month. That would be enough momentum to keep the national unemployment rate steady at 4.2%.

Most Fed officials are upbeat about labor conditions because unemployment trends remain historically low within the estimated bounds of full employment. The unemployment rate ticked up by just a tenth of a percentage point in September, and initial unemployment insurance claims have run at some of the lowest levels since the 1960s in recent weeks.

The Indeed Job Postings Index rose 0.3% in October, and the latest business surveys point to a stronger gain in payrolls over the past month. But new postings as defined by Indeed didn't improve in October.

ADP's measure of weekly private payrolls points to a monthly gain of around 65,000 jobs in October, down from September's reported advance of 90,000. The next ADP National Employment Report will be released Nov. 4.

LinkedIn reports that hiring in September remained 3.4% below its level of a year ago.

The data collectively point to a tight labor market, which stems largely from a lower supply of available workers. Restrictive immigration policies, deportations, and an aging workforce have shrunk the labor supply in the past few years, reducing hiring, which has kept the market in balance.

Although layoffs are relatively low, job prospects are challenging for the unemployed, writes Matthew Martin, senior U.S. economist at Oxford Economics. As of September, 27.1% of unemployed people had been jobless for more than 27 weeks, up from 24.7% in January.

The relative health of the labor market varies substantially by sector and even by region. Some sectors that once delivered reliable gains, such as healthcare and social assistance, are showing signs of slowing, while others aren't picking up the slack. Healthcare and social assistance, which includes support aides and social-work roles, have averaged 41,000 monthly job gains this year, down from an average monthly pace of 57,000 in 2025 and 74,000 in 2024.

Construction and manufacturing have reversed the hiring declines they saw over the past two years, both netting positive results since June. Still, the average monthly gain was only 18,000 year to date through September. The data-center buildout could lead to more gains in coming months, unless higher borrowing costs slow activity.

Policymakers may find themselves playing a tricky economic version of the classic game Operation. Can they remove the "ailment" of inflation without tripping the buzzer and further weakening the labor market? We'll find out in coming months if the Fed raises interest rates further.

Write to Megan Leonhardt at megan.leonhardt@barrons.com
